newsitem.title: FRANCE: French leftists want referendum on single currency.
newsitem.headline: French leftists want referendum on single currency.

text.p: The leader of the leftist Citizens' Movement party joined France's Communists on Wednesday to call for a referendum on whether France should adopt Europe's planned single currency, the Euro, due to be launched in 1999.

"The French people must be consulted on Europe and a transition to a single currency just as (President) Jacques Chirac proposed in November 1994, in the presidential campaign," Jean-Pierre Chevenement told a news conference.
Chevenement, who is president of the small left-wing party, the Citizen's Movement, served once as defence minister in a former Socialist government.
Chirac initially endorsed such a referendum, at time when he was a candidate in the 1995 presidential campaign. But he reversed his stance before the election took place.
Chevenement said his party had begun collecting signatures on a petition to be presented to Chirac on the matter.

The Communist Party launched a similar petition drive in January, saying citizens needed to be consulted on the question again, despite having narrowly approved the Maastricht treaty on European union in an earlier referendum.
